purpose: Per-stage executed evidence for the four source.mutex.guard.v1 CT cases this card mapped from card T03-F's proposals. Written in the same shape as docs/reports/remaining-t03-ct-integration/ct_stage_evidence.json so a future stage-derived summarizer can merge the three files instead of hand-maintaining the aggregate. T00's coverage.json is an archived audit at revision ea2af0f and is deliberately not rewritten here.
derivation_rule: A stage is `executed` only where a named workspace test runs it on the case's own artifact. A control fixture's execution is recorded under aux:, never as the case's own stage.
route: source.mutex.guard.v1 (qcore_frontend::source_mutex -> qcore_core::mutex_invariant), extended by card T03-F with bounded task composition, the `wait` announced acquisition and guard-scoped facts
route_has_no_cfg_stage: This route emits directly from the checked event list. There is no CFG construction, so `cfg` can never read `executed` for these cases and the manifest keeps it `unassessed`. CT03's `cfg: executed` precedent belongs to the task route, which reads `cfg` as the checked task IR it really builds; following it here would claim a stage that does not exist.
no_native_evidence_added: All four cases are rejections, so none reaches c_emission or native_execution. Three of the four accepted controls (CT28, CT31, CT32) are multi-task modules that the guard backend renders in no thread at all and that are therefore published checked with c_source: None (card T03-F section 3.5). CT48's accepted control is single-task and does emit C, but the harness route-checks every control rather than compiling it. The `evidence_target: linux` these cases carry records the harness's host gate — the Q500 non-Linux/macOS/Windows target refusal, which is evaluated before the emission decision — and NOT a compiled or executed run. No sanitized run, no schedule, no contention and no C memory-model claim is added by this card.

mutex_invariant_check.note: Rejection at Q612 WrongGuardAffinity, with the exact ordered cascade [Q612, Q600 JoinWhileGuardHeld] pinned. The second entry is load-bearing: it shows the refusal left the creator still holding the guard rather than silently releasing it.

aux:accepted_control.note: The same child takes its own acquisition of the same generation, writes under its own guard, and the creator reads after the join. Multi-task, so the guard backend renders it in no thread at all: it is published checked with c_source: None. The control is route-checked (as_checked_mutex_guards()), not compiled and not run; host_gate records the Q500 target refusal, which is evaluated before the emission decision.

aux:refused_control.note: The second half of the scenario name: the child unlocks the creator's guard (close g) instead of reading through it, and refuses with the identical [Q612, Q600] cascade, so guard affinity is keyed to the acting task and not to the operation kind.

mutex_invariant_check.note: Rejection at Q619 NonquiescentMutexDestruction, with the exact ordered cascade [Q619, Q600 NonquiescentDestruction, Q600 OutstandingMutex, Q600 OutstandingWaiter] pinned. Every entry after the first shows the refused destruction left the generation, the protected resource and the waiter outstanding rather than destroying one of them anyway.

aux:accepted_control.note: The announcing task performs the acquisition, and the core's Lock withdraws the waiter, so destruction is quiescent. Multi-task and `wait`-bearing (RegisterWaiter is in the emission-refused set), so it is published checked with c_source: None; route-checked, not compiled and not run.

mutex_invariant_check.note: Rejection at Q600 JoinWhileGuardHeld, cascade exactly one entry long. The length is the observation: the child body is empty and well formed, so a longer cascade would mean the refusal had also disturbed the guard or the generation.

aux:accepted_control.note: The identical child block, moved one statement past the section's end, checks. Multi-task, so it is published checked with c_source: None; route-checked, not compiled and not run.

mutex_invariant_check.note: Rejection at Q616 StaleProtectedFact, cascade exactly [Q616] because the release that dropped the fact was itself well formed. The binder is declared at thread-scope level, so the name resolves and the model refuses the use; a body-local binder would have produced the weaker Q013 unknown-name refusal the T03 CT integration report already recorded as insufficient.

aux:accepted_control.note: Re-establishing the refinement under the second guard mints a fresh fact and checks, so the spec's 'invalidate/re-establish, never assume' expectation is exercised in both directions. Single-task, so this control DOES emit C — the only one of the four this card adds that does — but the harness route-checks it and does not compile or run it.

aux:refused_control.note: A declared but never asserted fact refuses at Q600 UnknownFact, a different code from the case's Q616, so the case's diagnostic is keyed to a fact that existed and was dropped rather than to one that never existed.

cases_examined_and_left_unmapped.CT33: Lock-order cycle. Rank mode is a represented refusal in CheckedMutexInvariantV1, not a feature; there is no source form that declares a lock rank, so a cycle cannot be written down. Unchanged by card T03-F, which states this explicitly.
cases_examined_and_left_unmapped.CT34: Protected graph grows after creation. CreateMutex fixes its declared footprints at creation and there is no growth form; post-creation protection growth is refused rather than modelled.
cases_examined_and_left_unmapped.CT46: Needs Send/Sync derivation, which is outside L09 and outside this profile entirely.
